text: Tell me about a time you failed an exam, interview or competition and how you bounced back.
ideal_key_points: Specific setback described honestly | How they reflected on the reasons | Concrete steps taken to improve | Later outcome showing resilience

text: Tell me about a time you deployed an AI feature that produced harmful, biased or embarrassing outputs.
ideal_key_points: Specific feature and the problematic outputs | How it was detected and how fast they responded | Mitigation such as guardrails, filtering, evaluation sets or rollback | Communication with stakeholders | Changes to testing and responsible AI practices afterwards

text: Tell me about a task you took full ownership of from start to finish.
ideal_key_points: Specific task and its scope | Their end to end actions from planning to delivery | How they handled obstacles without waiting to be told | Result and impact

text: Describe a time you noticed a problem that was not your responsibility and fixed it anyway.
ideal_key_points: The problem and why it was outside their remit | Why they decided to act and how they informed owners | Actions taken | Outcome and whether it became a lasting fix

text: Tell me about a time you found a bug or data quality issue that others had missed.
ideal_key_points: How they spotted the issue, such as anomaly in metrics or data | Investigation to confirm and size the impact | Fix and communication to the team | Prevention such as validation checks or tests | Result in accuracy or reliability

text: Tell me about a time you went beyond the requirements of an assignment or project.
ideal_key_points: Original requirements stated clearly | What extra they did and why it added value | Kept the core deliverable on track | Recognition or measurable benefit

text: Tell me about a time you committed to something and could not deliver. How did you handle it?
ideal_key_points: Specific commitment and why it slipped | Communicated early and honestly with stakeholders | Offered a revised plan or partial delivery | Final outcome | What they changed in how they estimate or commit

text: Tell me about a time you cut a corner to save time and it came back to bite you.
ideal_key_points: Honest description of the shortcut and the reasoning | Consequences that followed | How they took responsibility and fixed it | Clear sense of which trade-offs are acceptable now | Specific habit adopted since

text: Walk me through how you solved a difficult technical problem in one of your projects.
ideal_key_points: Clear problem statement and constraints | Structured approach such as breaking down, hypotheses and testing | Alternatives considered and why the chosen one won | Result with concrete evidence

text: Tell me about a time you had to debug a model that was not learning or giving poor accuracy.
ideal_key_points: Specific symptoms such as flat loss or overfitting | Systematic checks such as data, labels, learning rate, baseline and leakage | Root cause found | Fix and measured improvement | Debugging habits they now follow

text: Describe a time you had very limited data or compute and still had to deliver an ML solution.
ideal_key_points: Concrete constraint and the goal | Creative strategies such as transfer learning, augmentation, smaller models or API use | Trade-offs explained | Result achieved within constraints | Lesson about resourcefulness

text: Tell me about a time you solved a problem with a simple approach instead of a complex model.
ideal_key_points: Problem and the tempting complex option | Why a simple baseline, rule or heuristic was chosen | Evidence that it worked, such as metrics or speed | Shows pragmatism and cost awareness

text: Tell me about a problem where you had to make a decision with incomplete information.
ideal_key_points: Situation and what information was missing | How they gathered what they could and assessed risk | The decision and the reasoning | Outcome and how they adjusted as more information came in

text: Tell me about a time you improved the speed, cost or efficiency of something you built.
ideal_key_points: Baseline performance or cost with numbers | How they found the bottleneck through profiling or measurement | Optimisation applied, such as caching, batching, quantisation or better queries | Measured improvement | Any trade-offs accepted

text: Tell me about the most complex problem you have worked on and why it was hard.
ideal_key_points: Problem with genuine complexity, not a tutorial task | Explains precisely what made it hard | Their own reasoning and key decisions | Result and remaining limitations acknowledged honestly | Depth that holds up to follow-up questions

text: Tell me about a time you took the initiative to start something new.
ideal_key_points: What they started, such as a project, club, tool or process | Why they saw the need | Steps to get buy-in and resources | Outcome and whether it continued

text: Describe a time you led a team, even informally, such as in a hackathon or college project.
ideal_key_points: Context and team size | How they set direction and divided work | How they handled a challenge in the team | Result such as a demo, rank or submission | What they learned about leading

text: Tell me about a time you introduced a new tool or practice to your team.
ideal_key_points: The tool or practice, such as experiment tracking, CI or code reviews | Problem it solved | How they convinced others and handled resistance | Adoption and measurable benefit

text: Tell me about a time you mentored or taught someone a technical skill.
ideal_key_points: Who they mentored and the skill | How they adapted the teaching to the person | Evidence the person improved | What mentoring taught them

text: Tell me about a time you had to lead without formal authority.
ideal_key_points: Situation needing leadership and no formal role | How they influenced through credibility, data or relationships | Handling of disagreement | Result achieved | Reflection on influence

text: Tell me about a time you proposed an idea that was rejected. What did you do next?
ideal_key_points: Idea and the reasoning behind it | How it was presented and why it was rejected | Accepted the decision gracefully and sought feedback | Whether they refined it later or moved on | Learning about pitching ideas

text: Tell me about a time you identified an opportunity to use AI to solve a real business or user problem.
ideal_key_points: Specific problem and who it affected | Why AI was the right fit rather than a buzzword | How they built a prototype or proof of concept | Impact measured or validated with users | Next steps or adoption

text: Tell me about a time you had to meet a very tight deadline.
ideal_key_points: Specific deadline and what was at stake | How they planned and prioritised | Result and whether it was met

text: How do you prioritise when you have several tasks due at the same time? Give an example.
ideal_key_points: Clear prioritisation method such as impact, urgency or dependencies | Real example with competing tasks | Communication with stakeholders about trade-offs | Outcome

text: Tell me about a time you realised midway that you would miss a deadline.
ideal_key_points: When and how they noticed the risk | Communicated early to stakeholders | Options offered such as scope cuts or extra help | Final outcome | Changes to planning since

text: Describe a time you had to cut scope to ship on time.
ideal_key_points: Original scope and deadline | How they decided what to cut based on value | Alignment with stakeholders | What shipped and its reception | Follow-up plan for deferred items

text: Tell me about a time you worked under pressure during a production issue or demo failure.
ideal_key_points: Specific high-pressure situation | How they stayed calm and triaged | Actions taken to recover | Outcome | Post-mortem or preventive steps

text: Tell me about a time you balanced academics or work with another big commitment.
ideal_key_points: Both commitments described | Time management approach | Result in both areas | What they learned about managing energy and time

text: Tell me about a time you delivered on time but compromised quality. Was it the right call?
ideal_key_points: Specific trade-off made under deadline | Honest assessment of the quality cost | Whether it was the right call with reasoning | How the technical debt was tracked and paid back | Nuanced view of speed versus quality

text: Describe a time you had to explain a technical result to a non-technical stakeholder.
ideal_key_points: Audience and what they needed to decide | Simplified without distorting, using analogies or visuals | Focused on business impact rather than jargon | Confirmed understanding and outcome of the conversation

text: Tell me about a time you had to explain why a model was not accurate enough or why AI was not the right fit.
ideal_key_points: Context and stakeholder expectations | Clear explanation of limitations such as data quality or error rates | Used concrete examples or metrics they could relate to | Offered alternatives or a path forward | Outcome and trust maintained

text: Tell me about a time a miscommunication caused a problem on your project.
ideal_key_points: What was misunderstood and the impact | Their role in the miscommunication | How it was resolved | Practice adopted to avoid it, such as written specs or recaps

text: Tell me about a presentation or demo you gave that went well. What made it effective?
ideal_key_points: Specific presentation and audience | How they prepared and structured it | Evidence it worked such as questions, feedback or decision | Takeaways for future presentations

text: Tell me about a time you wrote documentation that others relied on.
ideal_key_points: What was documented and why it was needed | How they made it clear and usable | Evidence others used it | Impact such as faster onboarding or fewer questions

text: Tell me about a time you had to give difficult feedback to a peer.
ideal_key_points: Situation and why feedback was needed | Prepared, specific and private delivery focused on behaviour | Listened to their side | Outcome and relationship afterwards

text: Tell me about a time you had to report bad news to a client or senior stakeholder.
ideal_key_points: Nature of the bad news and stakes | Delivered promptly and honestly without spin | Came with root cause and a recovery plan | Handled the reaction professionally | Outcome and lessons about transparency

text: Tell me about a project where you used a tool or framework you had never used before.
ideal_key_points: Tool or framework and why it was needed | How they learned it quickly, such as docs, examples or small prototypes | What they built | Lesson about learning on the job

text: How do you keep up with the fast pace of change in AI and machine learning?
ideal_key_points: Specific sources such as papers, blogs, courses or communities | Hands-on practice rather than only reading | Example of something recent they learned and applied | Filters hype from useful developments

text: Tell me about a time project requirements changed suddenly. How did you adapt?
ideal_key_points: Original plan and what changed | Initial reaction and how they re-planned | Reused work where possible | Outcome | Attitude toward change

text: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new domain such as finance, healthcare or retail to build an AI solution.
ideal_key_points: Domain and why understanding it mattered | How they learned, such as talking to experts or reading | How domain knowledge changed their technical approach | Result

text: Tell me about a time you had to unlearn something or change a strongly held opinion.
ideal_key_points: Belief held and why | What evidence or experience challenged it | How they updated their view | How it changed their work | Shows intellectual humility

text: Tell me about a time you had to switch tech stacks or migrate a project, for example from one LLM provider or framework to another.
ideal_key_points: Reason for the switch | How they planned the migration and managed risk | Problems encountered and solved | Outcome such as cost, quality or speed | Lesson about building adaptable systems

text: Tell me about a time you challenged an accepted way of doing things on your team and changed it.
ideal_key_points: Existing practice and its cost | Evidence gathered to make the case | How they persuaded others and handled resistance | Measurable improvement after the change | Reflection on picking battles wisely

text: Tell me about a time you received feedback that changed how you work.
ideal_key_points: Specific feedback and who gave it | Initial reaction, honestly described | Concrete behaviour change made | Evidence the change stuck and improved results | Shows genuine coachability

text: Tell me about a time you volunteered for a task nobody else wanted.
ideal_key_points: Task and why others avoided it | Why they took it on | How they completed it | Value it created for the team

text: Tell me about a time you used AI tools such as coding assistants or LLMs to solve a problem faster, and how you verified the output.
ideal_key_points: Specific problem and tool used | How it sped up the work | How they verified correctness, such as tests or review | Awareness of limitations such as hallucinations | Result

text: Tell me about yourself.
ideal_key_points: Concise present, past, future structure | Relevant education, projects or experience in AI and ML | One or two highlights with concrete results | Connects naturally to why they are interested in this role | Stays within about two minutes

text: Why do you want to work at our company?
ideal_key_points: Specific knowledge of the company's products, customers or AI work | Connects company needs to their own skills | Genuine reasons beyond salary or brand | Shows they researched rather than giving a generic answer

text: Why are you interested in this particular role?
ideal_key_points: Understanding of the role's responsibilities | Match between role and their skills and projects | What they hope to learn or contribute | Enthusiasm grounded in specifics

text: Why did you choose a career in AI and machine learning?
ideal_key_points: Personal and specific origin story | Sustained interest shown by projects, courses or work | Understanding of what the job actually involves beyond hype | Where they want to go within the field

text: What do you know about our company and what we do?
ideal_key_points: Accurate facts about business, products and customers | Awareness of recent news or AI initiatives | Opinion on where they could contribute | Asks or implies thoughtful curiosity

text: What kind of work environment helps you do your best work?
ideal_key_points: Honest description of preferred environment | Example of when they thrived in such conditions | Shows flexibility to adapt | Alignment with the company's actual culture

text: Would you prefer to work at a startup, a product company or a service company, and why?
ideal_key_points: Understands real differences in pace, ownership, scale and stability | Honest preference with reasons tied to their goals | Shows they would still fit and commit to this company | Avoids badmouthing any company type

text: Where do you see yourself in three to five years?
ideal_key_points: Realistic and specific growth goals | Connected to skills relevant to this role | Shows commitment to growing within the company | Mentions technical depth or leadership direction

text: What are your short-term and long-term career goals?
ideal_key_points: Clear short-term goal for the next year | Long-term direction that is plausible | Steps they are taking to get there | How this role fits the path

text: Do you see yourself on a technical track or a management track in the long run?
ideal_key_points: Honest preference with reasoning | Understanding of what each track involves | Openness to change with experience | Connection to current role

text: Would you be comfortable working on non-AI tasks such as data engineering, testing or maintenance if the project needed it?
ideal_key_points: Willingness to contribute where needed | Understands that real AI work includes data, testing and infrastructure | Example of doing such work before | Communicates own interests without being rigid

text: What are you currently learning, and why?
ideal_key_points: Specific topic or skill currently being learned | Why it matters for their goals or the role | How they are learning it, such as a project or course | Progress made so far

text: How would you explain a gap in your education or employment history?
ideal_key_points: Honest and brief explanation without over-justifying | What they did during the gap, such as learning, projects or caregiving | Shows readiness and recent relevant skills | Positive, forward-looking framing

text: You are switching careers into AI from another field. Why, and how have you prepared?
ideal_key_points: Clear and genuine reason for the switch | Concrete preparation such as courses, projects or certifications | Transferable skills from the previous field | Realistic expectations about starting level

text: What are your greatest strengths?
ideal_key_points: Two or three strengths relevant to the role | Each backed by a concrete example | Shows self-awareness rather than generic adjectives | Links strengths to value for the team

text: What is your biggest weakness?
ideal_key_points: Genuine weakness, not a disguised strength | Example of how it has affected work | Concrete steps taken to improve | Evidence of progress

text: How would your friends, classmates or colleagues describe you?
ideal_key_points: Few honest descriptors | Short examples supporting them | Includes how they work with others | Consistent with the rest of the interview

text: How do you handle constructive feedback or criticism?
ideal_key_points: Views feedback as useful and asks clarifying questions | Separates emotions from the content | Real example of acting on feedback | Follows up to show improvement

text: What is one skill you lack that would help you in this role, and what are you doing about it?
ideal_key_points: Names a real relevant skill gap | Explains why it matters for the role | Specific learning plan already in progress | Shows honesty without undermining their candidacy

text: Do you prefer working in a team or alone?
ideal_key_points: Honest preference with reasoning | Comfortable with both modes | Example of being effective in each | Recognises that AI projects need both deep focus and collaboration

text: Why should we hire you over other candidates?
ideal_key_points: Concise summary of relevant skills and results | Specific differentiator backed by evidence | Ties directly to the role's needs | Confident without being arrogant or criticising others

text: What are your salary expectations?
ideal_key_points: Researched market range for the role and location | Gives a range or reasonable figure with justification | Shows flexibility and interest in total compensation and growth | Professional tone without being evasive

text: What is your notice period, and can you join earlier if needed?
ideal_key_points: States notice period clearly and honestly | Mentions buyout or early release possibilities if any | Commits only to what is realistic | Shows respect for current employer obligations

text: Are you open to relocating or working from the office?
ideal_key_points: Clear and honest answer | Any constraints stated upfront | Flexibility where possible | Shows interest in the role regardless of location details

text: Are you comfortable with shift timings or working with clients in different time zones?
ideal_key_points: Honest about availability | Understands needs of global clients in service companies | Mentions any past experience | States constraints clearly if any

text: Do you have any other offers or interviews in progress?
ideal_key_points: Honest without disclosing unnecessary details | Explains where this company ranks and why | Gives a sense of their decision timeline | Avoids bluffing or pressure tactics

text: Are you willing to sign a service agreement or bond with the company?
ideal_key_points: Asks for or shows understanding of the terms | Honest about comfort level | Shows intent to stay and grow if committing | Professional and non-confrontational

text: Do you have any questions for us?
ideal_key_points: Asks thoughtful questions about the team, projects or AI roadmap | Asks about growth, mentoring or success in the role | Avoids questions answered by basic research | Avoids leading only with salary or leave

text: Imagine your manager asks you to use customer data to train a model without clear consent. What would you do?
ideal_key_points: Recognises the privacy, legal and trust risks, including India's data protection law | Raises concerns respectfully with the manager first | Suggests alternatives such as anonymisation, consent or synthetic data | Escalates through proper channels if needed | Does not quietly comply or overreact publicly

text: What would you do if you found that a model you built was biased against a group of users?
ideal_key_points: Takes it seriously and quantifies the bias | Informs the team and stakeholders | Investigates causes such as data imbalance | Proposes mitigation and ongoing fairness checks | Willing to delay launch if necessary

text: What would you do if you noticed a colleague copying code or results without attribution or faking metrics?
ideal_key_points: Verifies facts before acting | Speaks to the colleague privately first where appropriate | Escalates to a manager if serious or unresolved | Understands the impact on trust and product quality | Remains fair and professional

text: If you were under deadline pressure and your model's metrics were slightly below target, would you round them up in the report?
ideal_key_points: Clear no with reasoning about integrity | Reports actual numbers with context | Proposes a plan to close the gap | Communicates early with stakeholders

text: Suppose a client asks you to build an AI feature that you believe could mislead or harm end users. How would you respond?
ideal_key_points: Identifies the specific harm clearly | Raises concerns with the manager and client respectfully using evidence | Suggests safer alternatives such as disclosures or human review | Knows when to escalate or decline | Balances business needs with responsibility

text: How do you decide whether it is acceptable to paste company code or data into a public AI tool?
ideal_key_points: Checks company policy first | Considers confidentiality and data leakage risks | Uses approved or internal tools or removes sensitive data | Asks when unsure rather than assuming

text: What would you do if you realised you had made an error in a report that had already been shared with a client?
ideal_key_points: Informs the manager promptly | Assesses the impact of the error | Sends a correction transparently | Puts checks in place to prevent repeats
